the Vickers Hardness and the Ultimate Tensile Strength of SLM‐AlSi10M Mg can be improved by post‐heat treatment and that the Fracture Elongation is increased compared to the as‐built condition.
the mechanical properties of selectively laser‐meltd AlSi10Mn are improved via a post‐heat treatment consisting of solution annealing at 500 °C followed by precipitation hardening.

the Vickers microhardness and ultimate tensile strengths could not be improved by precipitation hardening, but a solution annealing at 550 °C reduces the Vickers hardness, the ultimate tensile strengths, and the fracture elongation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a post‐heat treatment which is able to improve the mechanical properties without the need for a time‐consuming solution annealing.
the influence of post‐treatment on the mechanical properties of additively manufactured AlSi10M.
the optimisation of post‐heat treatment parameters to improve the mechanical properties in the as‐fabricated state.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a heat treatment with a subsequent precipitation hardening is a promising method for the optimisation of the mechanical properties of AlSi10M.

a post‐heat treatment is possible and leads to a significant improvement in mechanical properties of SLS‐fabricated AlSi10M.
the mechanical properties of the as‐fabricated SLM‐AlSi10Mng alloy can be further optimised by post‐heat treatments.

the as‐fabricated material is suitable for applications where high strength and high ductility are not necessary, whereas a post‐treatment at 525 ° °C followed by a precipitation hardening is suitable for applications requiring high strength combined with a high fracture elongation.

the as‐fabricated material condition is superior in terms of ultimate tensile strength and fracture elongation, whereas the solution annealed and precipitation hardened condition is superior in hardness.
the mechanical characteristics of AlSi10Mn can be optimised by a combination of solution annealing and precipitation hardening.
